name: What Should I Check at the Final Kitchen Renovation Walkthrough?

mainEntity.name: What defects should I inspect before making the final payment on a kitchen remodel?
mainEntity.text: What defects should I inspect before making the final payment on a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a room-by-room checklist rather than judging the kitchen only by appearance. Open and close every door and drawer, test hardware alignment, inspect filler panels and toe kicks, and verify that cabinets are level and securely attached. Run water at all fixtures, check drains and shutoffs, test the disposal and dishwasher connection, and look for leaks. Test every outlet, switch, under-cabinet light, hood, appliance, and safety device. Inspect countertop seams, edges, sink mounting, backsplash joints, tile lines, grout, caulk, paint, floor transitions, trim, and wall repairs under both natural and task lighting. Confirm refrigerator, dishwasher, range, and oven doors open without hitting adjacent surfaces. Photograph defects and create a dated punch list with responsible parties and completion dates. Obtain final inspection records where applicable, appliance manuals, warranties, care instructions, spare materials, keys, and warranty contact information. Clarify how retained funds or final payment relate to incomplete items. Do not accept vague promises that defects will be fixed later; record the agreed remedy in writing.
acceptedAnswer.description: At the final walkthrough, test every cabinet door, drawer, appliance, outlet, switch, faucet, drain, light, hood, and shutoff. Check countertop seams, tile alignment, grout, caulk, paint, flooring, trim, and appliance clearances. Record unfinished or damaged work on a written punch list and confirm inspection approvals, manuals, warranties, and cleanup before final payment.
